evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. evidence.text: Backlog at Q3-end should be a record, and the company has effectively pre-disclosed it. Net of about $257M of Q3 revenue, that implies roughly $3.0-3.2B, against $2.36B.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed record backlog of $2.36B, up 137% y/y, and the stock moved -0.04%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because the contracts were announced individually and the release flagged the more than $1B of Q3 bookings. What is not public is the exact backlog figure and how much of it converts in the next 12 months (about 45% at Q2). A backlog well above about $3.1B would mean bookings beyond what was announced.
evidence.independence: The individual awards were reported separately: https://thedefensepost.com/2026/07/29/rocket-lab-us-launch-contract/ for the $266M award. The same company release underlies the backlog figure.

evidence.text: Electron cadence in Q3 was flat and Q4 so far is slow. Company and press counts give 12 launches by 2026-06-27 (mission 91), 16 by 09-11 (mission 95), 17 by 09-19 (mission 96) and mission 97 on 09-26 (Synspective), so Q3 had 6 missions, the same as Q1 (6 by 03-28) and Q2 (6). So Q3 revenue growth has to come from Space Systems, and the Q4 launch line looks modest.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 launch revenue fell about 30% q/q and the stock was flat on the print, so launch softness has not been punished when Space Systems carried the quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: Launch logs are public, but no preview I read gave a Q3 or Q4 launch count, and the Q3 guide already embeds the Q3 count, so that part sits inside the guide. The part that could matter is Q4: if it were priced, previews would flag a Q4 launch-revenue step-down, and none do.

evidence.text: The worst Neutron news was pre-released by 8-K on 2026-10-14: first launch moved to 2027 with no date, after voids were found in a carbon-composite Stage 1 forward dome, and the stock fell about 11% on 10-15. Since then the company says a replacement forward dome has been built and cured, and an aft dome made with the new process is described as its best yet. The call is the first chance to give a 2027 quarter. A firm H1 2027 date would relieve the stock; vagueness or another test issue would extend the drag.

evidence.why_not_priced: The delay itself is priced: it is in the 8-K and the stock fell 11%. What is not priced is the 2027 quarter, which the company has not given. Previews list a firmer date as the key test, so the market is uncertain about it, not positioned on it. Pre-releasing the bad news has historically left the call with less downside on this line.
evidence.independence: https://www.satellitetoday.com/launch/2026/10/15/rocket-labs-neutron-debut-now-delayed-to-2027/ and https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/rocket-lab-pushes-1st-launch-of-next-gen-neutron-rocket-to-2027 report the delay and the dome fix. evidence.text: AMD reported on 2026-11-03 and guided its Oct-Dec 2026 quarter to about $17bn revenue (+27% q/q, from $13.4bn). AMD is the customer behind Sanmina's ZT Systems manufacturing business and its next-generation AMD-based accelerated-compute program, which management in July pushed out of FQ4 into FQ1 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), the quarter Sanmina guides tonight. That supports a sequential step-up in the FQ1 guide and a reaffirmed or raised FY27 'more than $16bn' target.

evidence.why_not_priced: AMD reported six days ago, and SANM fell about 11% the next day in the midterm sell-off and kept falling to about $123-135. If the market were pricing AMD's Q4 rack ramp into Sanmina, SANM would have tracked AMD's post-print move, not sold off with data-center operators. Sanmina has not spoken since July, so consensus for its FQ1 predates AMD's Q4 guide.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/413880/sanminas-margin-gains-face-a-test-as-investors-look-past-q4-to-the-ai-ramp, 2026-11-02) confirms the next-gen AMD program ramp is 'slated to begin in fiscal Q1 2027'.
